title: A normalized principal boundary detects each component after regular base change
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain and $S$ a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $f:R\to S$ be a regular homomorphism, meaning flat with Noetherian geometrically regular residue-field fibres [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Fix $0\ne x\in R$ whose image $f(x)$ belongs to every maximal ideal of $S$. Let $E$ be the integral closure of $R$ in its field of fractions [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] and assume that $E$ is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For every minimal prime $P$ of $S$ there exist a prime $q$ of $S$ and a prime $Q$ of $E$ such that $P\subseteq q$, $f(x)\in q$, $Q$ is minimal among primes containing $xE$, and $f^{-1}(q)=Q\cap R$. A minimal prime means a prime with no strictly smaller prime. The conclusion is vacuous if $S$ is the zero ring.

source.place: Agent consequence of Tag 0BFK (lemma-normal-goes-up) after finite base change, with the principal ideal theorem and flat going-down. Compare Rotthaus, Zur Komplettierung ausgezeichneter Ringe (1980), printed p.223, component-retention argument beginning with the choice of K_1; here a finite normalization replaces the unnormalized principal boundary.
